messages:
devin: Quick check — we need a final decision on the internal API shape for telemetry + quota control. Two constraints: browser/console calls must be JSON-over-HTTP friendly, and service-to-service telemetry needs to be low-latency and cheap for high-cardinality traces. Thoughts?

maria: +1. TL;DR: browser -> REST JSON, service -> gRPC protobuf sounds reasonable, but we need a clear gateway pattern for translation so the console UX is consistent.

sahil: Agree, but we should decide where routing policy evaluation lives. If gateway evaluates it, we can return consistent quota headers to clients. If services evaluate it, we keep lower coupling.

olivia: Re: routing evaluation — leaning to centralized policy service (gRPC) with a light HTTP gate for browser. The gate can attach a signed policy token so backends don't need to re-eval for every request.

jamal: Would that require the gateway to be stateful? We want lightweight, autoscalable front doors. Signed token approach keeps gateway stateless (yay). But token size and TTL become important for policy churn.

maria: Example token flow I'd propose: gateway queries PolicySvc (gRPC) for a signed permit blob, caches it < 30s, returns to browser. Backend validates signature + TTL, applies local enforcement. Keeps both sides simple.

devin: That matches my mental model. Also want to decide on telemetry wire format for high-throughput metrics/traces — protobuf over gRPC gives compactness, but we need an ingest path that accepts JSON from the console. Gateway transcoding or a small adapter service?

sahil: Gateway transcoding is attractive but complicates gateway code. Alternative: tiny adapter that accepts JSON -> protobuf and forwards to TelemetryIngest (gRPC). Adapter can be trivial and autoscale separately.

olivia: Adapter also gives us transformation hooks (sampling, coarse aggregation) close to the edge, which helps reduce cardinality before it hits storage. Good for cost.

jamal: UX concern: console live-debug traces want very low latency SSE / WebSocket. gRPC-web might work, but browser compatibility and auth layers are messy. Maybe keep a thin JSON-over-WS path for live UI and push aggregated protobuf over gRPC for backend ingestion.

maria: +1. So final proposal: 1) Browser -> REST/WS (JSON) to Gateway/Adapter 2) Adapter -> TelemetryIngest (gRPC + proto) 3) PolicySvc (gRPC) authoritative for routing/quota decisions, returns signed permit tokens 4) Backends validate tokens and emit events to TelemetryIngest.

de vin: (typo) devin: small nit: call out where canary/fallback logic lives — if TelemetryIngest is overloaded, gateway should gracefully fallback to sampling mode and still serve console with degraded fidelity. We need a well-defined fallback signal.

console-bot: deploy.canary started: policy-svc v2 -> canary on 10% traffic (obs: latency baseline 18ms).

jamal: Good to see canary. For fallback signal, PolicySvc should emit explicit headers: `x-policy-mode: permit|sample|reject` and `x-policy-ttl`. Gateway + adapter act on these.

maria: Also add a console metric: `console.realtime.fidelity` so product can visualize degradation automatically. We should wire that into dashboards before GA.

devin: Action items: 1) sahil to prototype adapter (JSON->proto) + sample gateway hook (2 days) 2) maria to draft token format + TTL strategy (in RFC) 3) olivia to spec `x-policy-*` header set and failure modes 4) jamal to add metric to canary dashboard. Sync tomorrow 10am.

sahil: Acked. I'll drop a short repo with minimal code and a README with curl examples.

maria: I'll open RFC PR with token examples and validation pseudo-code.

olivia: I'll wire a dashboard panel in the console sandbox.

jamal: Thanks team. If we can keep the gateway stateless and push complexity into small adapters + PolicySvc, seems like best tradeoff for ops and rollout UX. :thumbsup:

devin: Cool — leaving this thread open for the PR links. If anyone sees a blocker call me.

console-bot: canary.alert: policy-svc v2 latency regressed +4ms, rolling back canary at 20% traffic.

maria: Noted — will pause token TTL changes until we validate.

devin: OK rollback acknowledged. We still proceed with adapter spike.

olivia: Sync added: invite sent to eng-platform + console + devex.
